name: Pastel Yellow
lede: Pastel Yellow is a pale, buttery [[yellow]] built by the modifier grammar "pastel + yellow", and our own sources disagree on exactly what it is.

sections.title: Two colors, one name
sections.body:
Our color library carries two records under this name. One, closer to a muted [[apricot|apricot]] gold (#EB9C52), traces to the RAL paint catalog and is placed by the ISCC-NBS 1955 lists in block 84 [1]. The other, the pale lemon shown here, comes from the xkcd 2010 crowd-name survey and is placed by ISCC-NBS in a different block as a "light greenish yellow" [1].

Books and standards bodies do not agree on a single referent for "pastel yellow"; this article follows the crowd-survey swatch, the one most people now picture [1]. In Munsell terms a precise match is not recorded for this swatch [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[banana]] and [[light-green-yellow]], at 3.4 and 3.5 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
This swatch is present, by lightness position within the painting, in 4 of our 23,781 paintings, with 6 found by raw coverage, as photographed [2]. That makes it rarer than 77% of the named colors we track [2].

In printed English, "pastel yellow" as a phrase peaks in the 2010s and rose fastest in the 2000s, matching its crowd-survey origin rather than any older paint-catalog use [2].
